sources.quote: Times/WTSP reporters used the FEC’s own data to identify roughly 100 zombie campaigns that have spent more than $20 million since 1995.
sources.searcher_note: The 2018 'zombie campaigns' investigation (year from URL); same pattern of dormant committees spending, but no 2024-cycle total or recipient-type share

sources.quote: Members of the 117th Congress who have since left Capitol Hill still hold nearly $54 million in leftover political money — cash they may tap to make contributions as lobbyists or bank for future runs.
sources.searcher_note: Stock of cash held by departed members, not 2024-cycle payouts

sources.quote: Crenshaw and Linder represent a twist in the zombie campaign story: both converted their campaign committees to multicandidate PACs, rolled-over hundreds of thousands of dollars of leftover contributions, and then used the PACs as slush funds.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: dormant committees routing money through PACs; case-level, no aggregate

sources.quote: Starting in July 2018, the Commission will examine the use of campaign funds by dormant committees as part of its review of campaign finance disclosure reports, to ensure the activity meets the regulatory standards for permissible use.
sources.searcher_note: FEC definition of dormant committees (House: no campaign or office for two years; Senate/president: four); no totals

sources.quote: Campaigns may also financially support party committees and their colleagues who are seeking to remain in office.
sources.searcher_note: Retiring lawmakers' surplus campaign spending in late 2025; pattern only, no share figures

notes: Only pattern coverage found (zombie or dormant campaign committees). No source reports a 2024-cycle total for old committees, the 189-committee count, the $8.57M figure, or the share going to candidates, parties and PACs (19.4% vs 2.1%).
